stories.title: Combatting adversarial distillation

sources.title: Combatting adversarial distillation
sources.title_en: Combatting adversarial distillation
sources.title_original: Combatting adversarial distillation
sources.recommend_reason_zh: OpenAI 介绍其对抗 adversarial distillation 的分层防护，并称 GPT‑6.2 Astra 与 GPT‑6.2 Sol 已强化 protected reasoning 防护，内部红队评估平均攻击成功率从 54.0% 降至 0.2%。

en.reason: OpenAI’s layered defenses against adversarial distillation, spanning model training, safeguards, detection and enforcement, cut internal red-team average attack success from 54.0% to 0.2% for GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol’s protected reasoning.

en.title: Microsoft CEO Nadella warns retailers that blocking AI shopping agents could cost them market share to open platforms like Shopify
en.reason: At The New York Times DealBook Summit on November 18, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella warned that retailers blocking third-party AI shopping agents, as Amazon does, risk losing market share to platforms like Shopify that only open checkout interfaces, undermining the human web model that depends on display advertising.

sources.recommend_reason_zh: OpenAI将GPT-6.2 Astra和GPT-6.2 Sol的推理提取成功率从54%压到0.2%，每周封禁数千至数万账号，对比Anthropic应对蒸馏攻击。

en.reason: OpenAI reduced successful extraction of protected internal reasoning from GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol from 54% to 0.2% in adaptive red-teaming tests and suspends thousands to tens of thousands of accounts weekly for coordinated distillation campaigns.

en.title: Damn — former Google CEO Eric Schmidt just spent 27 seconds laying out the easiest route to getting rich over the next two years. Making money, it turns out, is simple: start an agentic AI company, build an agent that can actually do real work, and own the whole thing yourself. From prompts, memory and skills to MCP, plus dev tools like Claude Code, one person can hand-build a company inside the one-to-two-year window. But after spending my days lately wrangling every kind of Agent workflow, I've grown increasingly clear-eyed: plenty of people are working themselves ragged building memory into AI, …
en.reason: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt’s 27-second path to wealth in the next two years centers on founding an agentic AI company you fully own, built solo with prompts, memory, skills, MCP and tools like Claude Code, while the piece warns that late nights, takeout and unchecked blood lipids and glucose can crash your body before your agent ships.

en.title: Agentic AI Architecture: Current Challenges and Future Opportunities
en.summary:
Agentic AI architecture extends microservices and cloud-native architecture by introducing AI agents that are context-aware, have memory, and follow protocols such as MCP and A2A. This article explores constrained context integration, coordination strategies for dependent tasks, emerging security risks, and observability requirements.

Word count: 4,253 | Reading time: about 14 minutes

AI is driving a paradigm shift in software architecture: from deterministic data processing systems to intelligent systems that incorporate knowledge reasoning. Architects and engineers must rethink design, testing, and operations methodologies to accommodate the introduction of non-deterministic AI components. The role of IT systems is evolving from "data pipelines" to "knowledge collaborators."

AI extends IT system capabilities from operating on data to operating on knowledge
Non-deterministic AI components require rethinking traditional architecture governance and observability practices
Knowledge worker products are becoming the first key scenarios for AI architecture implementation
Intended for cloud-native architects, platform engineering leads, and technical leads of AI engineering teams

Most software engineers and architects are already familiar with microservices and cloud-native architecture and have spent years building on them…
en.reason: Agentic AI architectures extend microservices and cloud-native designs with context-aware, memory-enabled agents using MCP and A2A; coverage spans constrained-context integration, dependent-task coordination, security risks, observability, and Google/MIT findings that financial reasoning favors centralized orchestration while web navigation suits decentralized strategies.

sources.title_original: Entire Git Forge：面向编码智能体重构 Git 协作方式
sources.summary:
Entire 是面向开发者与 AI 编码智能体协同的 Git 代码托管平台，它认为传统开发基建（特别是PR流程）无法适配AI智能体高速生成、评审和迭代代码的模式。
Entire 是面向开发者与 AI 编码智能体协同的 Git 代码托管平台，它认为传统开发基建（特别是PR流程）无法适配AI智能体高速生成、评审和迭代代码的模式。
本文字数：1397 字
阅读完需：约 5 分钟
Entire 是面向 AI 智能体与人类协同开发的新型 Git 托管平台，重构了 PR 流程以适配多智能体高频迭代场景。其核心是 trails（轨迹）机制，通过置顶式评估分数驱动合并决策，取代传统线性时间线。平台基于全分布式架构，代码推送性能达 GitHub 的 89 倍。
Trail 将关键评估指标（置信度、风险、问题状态）结构化呈现；PR 合并决策由量化分数而非人工阅读日志驱动；全分布式架构原生支持高并发智能体协作。
适合 AI 编程基础设施工程师、DevOps 架构师、AI Agent 系统开发者阅读。

sources.recommend_reason_zh: Entire 用 trails 置顶展示置信度、风险等评估分数来驱动 PR 合并，其全分布式架构代码推送速度最高达 GitHub 的 89 倍。

en.title: Entire Git Forge: Rethinking Git Collaboration for Coding Agents
en.summary:
Entire is a Git code hosting platform built for developers working alongside AI coding agents. Its core argument: traditional development infrastructure — especially the PR workflow — can't accommodate how fast AI agents generate, review, and iterate on code.

Word count: 1,397. Reading time: about 5 minutes.

Entire is a new Git hosting platform for collaborative development between AI agents and humans, rebuilding the PR workflow for the high-frequency iteration of multi-agent scenarios. At its core is the trails mechanism, which drives merge decisions through pinned evaluation scores instead of the traditional linear timeline. The platform runs on a fully distributed architecture and delivers code push performance 89x that of GitHub.

A trail presents key evaluation metrics — confidence, risk, and issue status — in a structured format. PR merge decisions are driven by quantified scores rather than humans reading through logs. The fully distributed architecture natively supports high-concurrency agent collaboration.

Intended for AI programming infrastructure engineers, DevOps architects, and AI Agent system developers.

Entire is a Git code hosting platform designed specifically for collaboration between human developers and AI coding agents. Its core view is that
en.reason: Entire, a Git hosting platform built for collaboration between developers and AI coding agents, replaces linear PR timelines with pinned trails that surface confidence and risk scores to drive merge decisions, and its fully distributed architecture pushes code up to 89 times faster than GitHub.

en.title: Entire Git Forge: Rethinking Git Collaboration for Coding Agents
en.summary:
Entire is a Git code hosting platform built for developers working alongside AI coding agents. Its core argument: traditional development infrastructure — especially the PR workflow — can't accommodate how fast AI agents generate, review, and iterate on code.

Word count: 1,397. Reading time: about 5 minutes.

Entire is a new Git hosting platform for collaborative development between AI agents and humans, rebuilding the PR workflow for the high-frequency iteration of multi-agent scenarios. At its core is the trails mechanism, which drives merge decisions through pinned evaluation scores instead of the traditional linear timeline. The platform runs on a fully distributed architecture and delivers code push performance 89x that of GitHub.

A trail presents key evaluation metrics — confidence, risk, and issue status — in a structured format. PR merge decisions are driven by quantified scores rather than humans reading through logs. The fully distributed architecture natively supports high-concurrency agent collaboration.

Intended for AI programming infrastructure engineers, DevOps architects, and AI Agent system developers.

en.reason: Entire, a Git hosting platform built for collaboration between developers and AI coding agents, replaces linear PR timelines with pinned trails that surface confidence and risk scores to drive merge decisions, and its fully distributed architecture pushes code up to 89 times faster than GitHub.

sources.title_original: Cops Are Pushing Extremely Corny ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Slop
sources.summary:
The blockbuster game makes no secret of its contempt for law enforcement. Real police departments using it to recruit new members and scold the public apparently didn’t get the memo.

sources.recommend_reason_zh: 文章讲San Diego Police Department借Grand Theft Auto VI发售发AI生成巡逻车图并配“Join San Diego PD VI”招募，还提到Glendale Police Department用“Keep It In The Game VI”提醒现实限速，呈现真实警局蹭游戏热度的尴尬。

en.reason: San Diego Police Department used an AI-generated patrol-car image and “Join San Diego PD VI” to recruit new members, while Glendale Police Department’s “Keep It In The Game VI” reminded drivers of real-world speed limits.

stories.title: 7 个小时 21 元，用 DeepSeek Harness 操控手机，复刻所有 APP！

sources.title: 7 个小时 21 元，用 DeepSeek Harness 操控手机，复刻所有 APP！

sources.summary: 想低成本用 Agent 复刻 App 的开发者可以参考这套落地方案。作者依托 DeepSeek Harness，采用净室复刻思路，通过 ADB 真机采集解析界面，完整复刻了 Gemini Flow，花费了7个小时仅21元就跑通了全部功能。
sources.recommend_reason_zh: 作者花 7 个小时、21 元，用 DeepSeek Harness 复刻出能生成图片视频、编辑与延长视频的 Gemini Flow，并放出 FlowClone 与原版 Google Flow 的高保真对比合集。

en.title: 7 hours and 21 yuan: using DeepSeek Harness to control a phone and replicate every app
en.summary: Developers looking to replicate an app with an Agent on a low budget can refer to this implementation approach. Using DeepSeek Harness and a clean-room replication strategy, the author captured and parsed the interface via ADB on a real device, fully replicating Gemini Flow and getting every feature working in 7 hours for just 21 yuan.
en.reason: Using DeepSeek Harness and ADB-based real-device interface capture, the author clean-room replicated Gemini Flow's image/video generation, editing and extension features in 7 hours for 21 yuan, publishing FlowClone alongside high-fidelity comparisons with Google Flow.

en.title: AI memory is helping me — and also seems to trap me
en.summary: AI memory brings convenience, but it also carries a hidden risk of trapping people. After the author added a "novice lecturer" tag, the AI kept limiting opportunities to the training track, reinforcing the stereotype and even leading the author to gradually identify with this single identity. This reflection is a warning for heavy Agent users: in human-AI coexistence, don't let AI's memory box in your broader potential.

en.title: How do you test AI visibility in GEO? Recording cards as a case study
en.summary: To find out whether AI will proactively recommend your product, this reusable AI visibility testing method is worth a look. Using Notta Memo’s overseas market test as a case study and drawing on NIST and IAB industry standards, the author explains prompt design, variable control, result evaluation, baseline retention, and retesting logic, with a logging template included.
en.reason: Using Notta Memo's US-English launch as a case study, the piece lays out a reusable GEO testing method built on NIST and IAB standards, covering prompt design, variable control, distinguishing brand mentions from product recommendations, and baseline logs for retesting.

en.title: Let AI add visuals to voiceovers: I built an infinitely reusable open-source Skill (with hands-on tests of 6 models)
en.summary: Anyone looking to build an automated short-form news video pipeline shouldn't miss this Skill from Azhen. After hands-on testing across several major LLMs, she found that you just feed it a script and it automatically generates matching visuals, with stable layout and flexible motion effects—no repeated debugging each time. Worth giving it a try!

en.title: For everyone saying GPT6.2 is no good, Lao Jin has a secret playbook
en.summary: GPT-6.2 Astra's performance is sharply divided. This article breaks down four typical categories of problems while also comparing its cost advantages and the use cases it fits.
en.reason: Two days after GPT-6.2 Astra launched, users reported it spent two hours on an Outer Wilds level without delivering while asking for a filename, and the piece explains four such problems, fixes, cost advantages and suitable scenarios.

en.title: Here's a dry joke for you: some universities in China have started offering AI 🤖 courses. Given how fast AI is moving these days, I'm curious what they actually teach. A new agent or a new model pops up every day—so what goes into the theory classes, and what goes into the practical ones?
en.reason: Chinese universities that have launched AI courses face a curriculum question as new agents and models emerge daily, raising doubts about what theory and practice classes can still teach at that pace.

sources.recommend_reason_zh: 去哪儿郑吉敏、帆软张驰、Fabarta谭宇从业务实践、AI产品孵化与客户现场出发，聊个人提效后团队协作和管理机制如何跟上，以及需求理解、人才培养与项目经验沉淀。

en.title: With AI here, how exactly do teams change?
en.reason: Qunar’s Zheng Jimin, Fanruan’s Zhang Chi and Fabarta’s Tan Yu discuss how team collaboration and management mechanisms must catch up after individual AI productivity gains, covering requirement understanding, talent development and turning project success into reusable organizational capability.

Title: Chrome给AI编程助手塞了203篇前端规范，我拆包实测：检索0.77秒是真快，扫描器有点挑食
Published Time: 2026-11-18T12:37:00+00:00
掘金热榜最近有个现象挺有意思：大厂官方仓库成批上榜，带的几乎都是给AI编程助手看的规范文件，有篇盘点说这类仓库最近一周在热榜占了32席。这里面动静最大的是Chrome的Modern Web Guidance——11月10日出到1.0，Edge、Firefox、MDN团队也进了维护名单，等于四大浏览器系一起给"AI该怎么写前端"定了调。
我对此一直有个疑问：这类规范包到底是个什么成色的东西？宣传语都差不多，"把现代Web最佳实践塞进你的coding agent"，听着像一份精装修的prompt合集。决定它价值的是细节：指南内容是文档还是指令？检索是噱头还是真基础设施？扫描器到底能不能认出老代码？热榜上的文章都停在盘趋势，没人拆开看。正好这玩意一条npx命令就能跑，我直接把它拆了一遍。
先看体积：npm上的包16.5MB，版本1.0.0。装进去（npx会缓存到本地）翻目录，结构比我想的简单：
mo
sources.recommend_reason_zh: 作者拆包实测Chrome的Modern Web Guidance 1.0：npm包16.5MB，检索0.77秒，指南是带版本兼容性边界的硬指令；但legacy-scan仅35条规则覆盖33篇指南约20%，文件级守卫会让::-webkit-scrollbar命中归零。

en.title: Chrome Stuffed 203 Frontend Style Guides Into Its AI Coding Assistant. I Cracked It Open and Tested It: 0.77-Second Retrieval Is Genuinely Fast, but the Scanner Is a Bit Picky
en.summary:
Chrome Stuffed 203 Frontend Specs Into Its AI Coding Assistant. I Unpacked It: 0.77-Second Retrieval Is Legit Fast, but the Scanner Is a Bit Picky

Something interesting has been happening on the Juejin trending list: official big-company repos are hitting the charts in batches, and nearly all of them ship spec files written for AI coding assistants. One roundup counted 32 such repos on the trending list in the past week. The loudest one is Chrome's Modern Web Guidance—it hit 1.0 on November 10, and the Edge, Firefox, and MDN teams have joined the maintainer list, meaning all four major browser camps have together set the tone for how AI should write frontend code.

I've had one question all along: what exactly is this kind of spec package made of? The pitch is always the same—"put modern web best practices into your coding agent"—and it sounds like a nicely packaged prompt collection. What decides its value is the details: is the guide content documentation or instructions? Is retrieval a gimmick or real infrastructure? Can the scanner actually recognize legacy code? Every article on the trending list stops at analyzing the trend; nobody opens the thing up. Since it runs with a single npx command, I just took it apart.

First, size: the npm package is 16.5MB, version 1.0.0. After installing it (npx caches it locally) and poking through the directory, the structure is simpler than I expected.
en.reason: Chrome's Modern Web Guidance 1.0 packs 203 front-end guidelines into a 16.5MB npm package, with the author measuring 0.77-second retrieval but finding legacy-scan's 35 rules cover about 20% and a file-level guard zeroes out ::-webkit-scrollbar hits.

en.summary:
Chrome Stuffed 203 Frontend Specs Into Its AI Coding Assistant. I Unpacked It: 0.77-Second Retrieval Is Legit Fast, but the Scanner Is a Bit Picky

Something interesting has been happening on the Juejin trending list: official big-company repos are hitting the charts in batches, and nearly all of them ship spec files written for AI coding assistants. One roundup counted 32 such repos on the trending list in the past week. The loudest one is Chrome's Modern Web Guidance—it hit 1.0 on November 10, and the Edge, Firefox, and MDN teams have joined the maintainer list, meaning all four major browser camps have together set the tone for how AI should write frontend code.

I've had one question all along: what exactly is this kind of spec package made of? The pitch is always the same—"put modern web best practices into your coding agent"—and it sounds like a nicely packaged prompt collection. What decides its value is the details: is the guide content documentation or instructions? Is retrieval a gimmick or real infrastructure? Can the scanner actually recognize legacy code? Every article on the trending list stops at analyzing the trend; nobody opens the thing up. Since it runs with a single npx command, I just took it apart.

First, size: the npm package is 16.5MB, version 1.0.0. After installing it (npx caches it locally) and poking through the directory, the structure is simpler than I expected.

Title: 我又用 AI 做了个小程序：24 天，记录我这辈子认识的人
Published Time: 2026-11-20T02:16:25+00:00
上个月我妈打电话，问我三舅姥爷家那个孩子今年是不是高考。
我张了张嘴，名字在嘴边，就是说不出来。最后翻了十分钟微信，才在一个八百年没人说话的群里找到他的名字。
那一下挺难受的。这些人我明明都见过，一起吃过饭，被叫过哥，敬过酒。但除了一个模糊的脸，什么都不剩。
我试过记在备忘录里。记到三十来条就乱了：这条是老王的，那条是大学室友的，搜「火锅」能搜出一堆人。微信聊天记录也不行，它只留说过的话，不留「这人胃不好，吃不了辣」。
我想要的其实很朴素：一个人一页纸。他生日几号、我们怎么认识的、这几年一起干过什么，想翻的时候能翻到。
这不是我第一次做小程序。之前做过一个电子同学录，毕业季用，每个人扫码进去写自己那一页。
但同学录只记得住一场毕业。毕业三年、五年之后，那些人一年一年地散掉，我连名字都快想不起来了。
所以我又开了一个。同一套「一人一页」的想法，从记一场毕业，变成记一辈子认识的人。
只是「朴素的东西」，一个人做不出来。要设计，我不会画

en.summary:
I Built Another Mini Program with AI: 24 Days to Record Everyone I've Ever Known

Last month my mom called to ask whether the kid in my great-uncle's family was taking the college entrance exam this year.

I opened my mouth. The name was right there on the tip of my tongue, but it wouldn't come out. In the end I scrolled through WeChat for ten minutes before finding it in a group chat that hasn't seen a message in ages.

That one hurt. I've met all these people — we've eaten together, they've called me "bro," we've raised glasses to each other. But all that's left is a blurry face and nothing else.

I tried keeping notes in my memo app. By around thirty entries it fell apart: this one's about Old Wang, that one's a college roommate; search "hot pot" and you get a pile of people. WeChat chat logs don't work either — they only keep what was said, not "this guy has a bad stomach and can't handle spicy food."

What I wanted was actually pretty simple: one page per person. Their birthday, how we met, what we've done together over the years — something I can pull up when I want it.

This isn't my first mini program. I made a digital yearbook before, for graduation season — everyone scans a code and writes their own page.

But a yearbook only captures one graduation. Three, five years out, those people scatter year by year, and I can barely remember their names.

So I started another one. Same "one page per person" idea, but instead of one graduation, it's everyone I'll ever know.

Except "simple things" aren't something one person can build alone. There's design — I can't draw

Title: 我又用 AI 做了个小程序：24 天，记录我这辈子认识的人
Published Time: 2026-11-20T02:16:25+00:00
上个月我妈打电话，问我三舅姥爷家那个孩子今年是不是高考。
我张了张嘴，名字在嘴边，就是说不出来。最后翻了十分钟微信，才在一个八百年没人说话的群里找到他的名字。
那一下挺难受的。这些人我明明都见过，一起吃过饭，被叫过哥，敬过酒。但除了一个模糊的脸，什么都不剩。
我试过记在备忘录里。记到三十来条就乱了：这条是老王的，那条是大学室友的，搜「火锅」能搜出一堆人。微信聊天记录也不行，它只留说过的话，不留「这人胃不好，吃不了辣」。
我想要的其实很朴素：一个人一页纸。他生日几号、我们怎么认识的、这几年一起干过什么，想翻的时候能翻到。
这不是我第一次做小程序。之前做过一个电子同学录，毕业季用，每个人扫码进去写自己那一页。
但同学录只记得住一场毕业。毕业三年、五年之后，那些人一年一年地散掉，我连名字都快想不起来了。
所以我又开了一个。同一套「一人一页」的想法，从记一场毕业，变成记一辈子认识的人。
只是「朴素的东西」，一个人做不出来。要设计，我不会画

sources.summary:
Title: 给Deepseek Harness装上插件市场，从此插件无忧
Published Time: 2026-11-19T05:19:39+00:00
前阵子折腾 `DeepSeek Harness`（下面简称 `DSH`），想给 `dsh web` 装几个社区插件。流程不复杂，就是敲命令：
dsh plugin --profile web add 某个包名
遇到名字相同的总会搜多失败或者不知道是哪个。
近来发现一个项目`dsh-market`，一个可视化商店。装插件从此无忧，找插件更直观。
`dsh-market`是长在 `DeepSeek Harness` 内部的一个插件市场插件。不是独立网站，不是独立`App`，是宿主进程里的一个 `cordis` 插件，同时注入一份 `React` 客户端到宿主的`Web UI`里。
在 `dsh 0.2.1+`，它表现为 `Plugins` 页面里紧挨着 `Installed` 的一个页签；老版本则藏在 `Settings → Plugin Market`。核心就三件事：浏览、搜索、一键安装。
更是已经拥有`12.1k`的`star`
sources.recommend_reason_zh: 文章介绍已获12.1k star的dsh-market：它作为DeepSeek Harness内部的cordis插件注入Web UI，提供浏览、搜索、一键安装，并涵盖安装编排、热禁用、崩溃自救、备份恢复与诊断修复。

en.title: Add a plugin marketplace to Deepseek Harness and never worry about plugins again
en.summary:
DeepSeek Harness gets a plugin marketplace, and plugin hassles are over

Not long ago I was tinkering with `DeepSeek Harness` (DSH for short), trying to install a few community plugins for `dsh web`. The process wasn't complicated — just type:

dsh plugin --profile web add some-package-name

But when names overlapped, searches would often fail or I couldn't tell which package was which.

Recently I came across a project called `dsh-market`, a visual storefront. Installing plugins is now painless, and finding them is far more intuitive.

`dsh-market` is a plugin marketplace plugin that lives inside `DeepSeek Harness`. It's not a standalone website or app — it's a `cordis` plugin in the host process that also injects a `React` client into the host's `Web UI`.

On `dsh 0.2.1+` it shows up as a tab right next to `Installed` on the `Plugins` page; on older versions it's tucked under `Settings → Plugin Market`. It does three core things: browse, search, one-click install.

It already has `12.1k` stars.
en.reason: dsh-market, a 12.1k-star cordis plugin living inside DeepSeek Harness that injects a React client into its Web UI, adds a Plugins tab in dsh 0.2.1+ for browsing, searching and one-click installing community plugins.

en.reason: Signal now blocks in-app screenshots by default on iOS 27 and auto-enables Screen security on some Android phones when AI screen-reading is detected, after Reuters tests showed Meta's Muse reading Signal messages via notifications, accessibility tools and screenshots.

en.title: AI dev tool selection through Trellis: how OpenSpec, Spec Kit, and Harness work together
en.reason: Teams running Codex, Cursor and Claude Code together hit duplicated rule versions, missed scenarios and lost session progress, and this piece uses a voice-chat-room auto-reconnect case to separate what Spec Kit, OpenSpec, Harness, Trellis and Rulesync each handle.
